objective: Introduce focused internal same-directory atomic write primitives for text and PyTorch artifacts without changing existing artifact writers or public training APIs yet.
acceptance_criteria: A new internal training artifact I/O module provides text and PyTorch-save operations that write to a uniquely named temporary file in the destination directory, flush and fsync completed bytes, and publish with os.replace.

If serialization, flush, fsync, or replace fails before publication, an existing destination remains byte-for-byte unchanged and the helper makes a best-effort cleanup of its own temporary file without masking the original exception.
Successful publication leaves no helper-owned temporary file and produces content loadable through the corresponding standard text or torch.load path.
The helpers do not fall back to another directory, do not delete or reuse pre-existing arbitrary files, and do not claim multi-file transactional semantics.
The module remains internal and does not alter Phase 6 or Phase 7 public controller, worker, request, result, training workflow, model-definition, or dataset APIs.

Focused CPU-only tests use temporary directories and fault injection to cover success, preservation of an existing destination, replace failure, serializer failure, cleanup, Unicode text, and shell=False/network-free behavior.
No existing artifact writer is migrated in this checkpoint and no later-checkpoint documentation or bundle transaction format is introduced.
claude_prompt: Implement only Phase 8 checkpoint 1 in the two allowed files. Add a small internal artifact_io module with same-directory temporary-file plus flush/fsync/os.replace primitives for UTF-8 text and torch serialization, following the repository's proven checkpoint/imagefolder-resume safety patterns without changing those existing modules. Preserve an existing destination on every pre-publication failure, clean up only the helper-created temporary file, propagate the original error, and explicitly avoid claiming a transaction across multiple artifacts. Add focused CPU-only fault-injection tests. Do not migrate save_model_spec, save_class_mapping, or save_state_dict yet; that is checkpoint 2. Do not modify public APIs, GUI, workflow, docs, goals, config, dependencies, or unrelated code. Do not use actual CUDA, models, external network, Bash, or Git; do not commit or push; do not claim unexecuted tests; do not implement later checkpoints or unrelated refactors.
estimated_scope: Small internal infrastructure slice: one new training utility and one focused test module, approximately 140-240 changed lines combined.
